sources.authority_reason: Gneiting and Raftery are the paper authors; author-hosted copy of the 2007 JASA article.
sources.inspection_note: Read p.359 and §2.1 Eq.(1), then §3.1 Examples 1 and 3 on pp.362–363. The paper uses reward maximization; negating log score and quadratic score gives the lesson’s minimized CE and sum-of-class-squares Brier. It explicitly labels both strictly proper. Population expectation and true outcome distribution are the conditions, rather than a finite training-set guarantee.

sources.inspection_note: Read §2 Eq.(1) (conditional correctness calibration), Eq.(6) (NLL), §3 NLL/accuracy disconnect, §4 held-out validation and common-distribution assumptions, and §4.2 Eq.(9). T is a shared positive scalar; selection minimizes validation NLL and the argmax remains unchanged. The finite grid in this lesson/9.10 is a declared approximation, not a claim of the paper’s continuous optimum. No paper figure or benchmark result is used as a claim about this project.

sources.title: Transparent probability and loss derivations
sources.details: D1: Hypothetical 40 correct out of100 means40/100=0.4, compared with stated0.8, a0.4 absolute frequency gap; this is not measured project data. D2: For normalized q and p, CE(q,p)=-Σq_i log p_i; with q=e_k all zero-weight terms vanish (usual0log0 convention), giving-log p_k. For Bernoulli y, q=(y,1-y), giving-[ylog p+(1-y)log(1-p)]. D3: For true distribution r, E[-log p_Y]-E[-log r_Y]=Σr_i log(r_i/p_i)=KL(r||p)>=0. For Brier sum, E[Σ(p_i-1{Y=i})²]=Σ(p_i-r_i)²+1-Σr_i², so the unique population minimum is p=r. These are the loss-oriented versions of s_proper. Finite empirical risk, a restricted model class or noisy labels need not attain the true target r. D4: Positive shared T preserves each comparison z_i>z_j iff z_i/T>z_j/T; exp and shared normalization preserve it, hence the argmax set (and a consistent tie rule). This is a mathematical statement, not an all-extreme-float guarantee or a cross-example confidence-order claim. D5: All predictions p_max=0.7 can be population-calibrated overall when equal-sized groups have correctness1 and0.4: (1+0.4)/2=0.7, while neither subgroup has correctness0.7. D6: The same constant uniform probability vector for all inputs contains no input-dependent class ranking. On balanced three-class data it may be calibrated with1/3 accuracy; its calibration therefore does not establish discrimination or lower task cost. D7: The three-class one-hot losses are -ln0.8≈0.22314355 and -ln0.2≈1.60943791; Brier sums0.2²+0.1²+0.1²=0.06 and0.8²+0.7²+0.1²=1.14. Uniform CE=-ln(1/3)=ln3≈1.09861229 and Brier4/9+1/9+1/9=2/3≈0.66666667. These derivations are kept distinct from the actual float32 execution in a_execution.
